title: Secure Enclave Processor (SEP) Firmware & Hardware Security Analysis
architecture: ARM64e / Apple Custom Secure Core (AArch64 with PAC & Hardware Crypto Isolation)

associated_manifest_files.description: Restore identity verification manifest declaring production (sepi) and research (rsep) SHA-384 digests and base64 TBMDigests.
Stage-1 early boot microkernel patches for SEPOS exception handlers and errata workarounds.
Stockholm embedded Secure Element (eSE) JCOP SmartCard OS firmware managed by SEPOS via APDU/SPI channels.

memory_regions.execution_model: Two-Tier Cryptographic Architecture (Isolated On-Chip SRAM & Hardware-Filtered Secure DRAM)

tz0.name: TrustZone 0 (TZ0) Primary Secure DRAM Carveout
tz0.bus_filtering: Apple Memory Controller (AMC) hardware address filter (cpu-ctrl-filtered). Blocks all Application Processor (AP) bus masters, hypervisors, and DMA controllers.
tz0.purpose: SEPOS microkernel runtime code, kernel data structures, thread control blocks, cryptographic context cache, and biometric template staging.

tz1.name: TrustZone 1 (TZ1) Protected Carveout Window
tz1.bus_filtering: Protected peripheral window filtered by DART-SEP and Exclave memory partitions.
tz1.purpose: High-bandwidth secure sensor pipelines (Pearl Face ID raw IR frame staging) and ExclaveCore secure memory isolation windows.

internal_sram.protection: Hardware ECC (Error-Correcting Code) with parity trap generation

components.name: Secure Boot ROM
components.description: Immutable silicon ROM holding the primary bootloader, hardware public root key, and initial RSA/ECDSA verification engine.

components.name: L1 Cache Array
components.description: Dedicated L1 instruction (64 KB) and L1 data (64 KB) caches physically isolated from AP cores.

components.name: L2 Unified Cache
components.description: Internal 1 MB secure L2 cache backed by inline hardware encryption.

components.name: Cryptographic Key Scratchpad
components.description: Zero-leakage internal SRAM registers for intermediate AES and PKA operations, cleared upon core reset.

mappers.name: mapper-sep
mappers.purpose: Standard AP-to-SEP bulk DMA shared memory buffers (OOL buffers, relay buffers, and crash dump telemetry).

mappers.name: mapper-sep-mpm
mappers.purpose: Multi-Power Management (MPM) sleep and wake memory staging, retaining low-power context during AP deep idle.

mappers.name: mapper-sep-exclave
mappers.purpose: ExclaveCore microkernel secure memory mapping channel, bypassing AP kernel execution.

peripheral_mmio_mappings.role: Apple ASCwrap-v6 Mailbox MMIO: Inbox/Outbox FIFO data words, status flags, doorbell triggers, and interrupt management.
Secure Enclave Power Manager (SEPM), secure clock gating, sleep state controllers, hardware timers, and watchdog monitors.
Biometric Face ID sensor hardware interface mapping ISP (isp_map_iobmd) and ANE (ane_map_iobmd) buffers directly into SEP memory space.

interrupt_lines.name: OUTBOX_NOT_EMPTY
interrupt_lines.description: Asserted by SEP hardware when an outbound message word is placed in the outbox FIFO for AP consumption.

interrupt_lines.name: INBOX_EMPTY
interrupt_lines.description: Asserted when the AP-to-SEP inbox FIFO has drained and is ready to accept new message words.

interrupt_lines.name: DOORBELL_STATUS
interrupt_lines.description: Hardware doorbell synchronization interrupt signaling command completion or state transition.

interrupt_lines.name: ERROR_FAULT
interrupt_lines.description: Hardware exception interrupt signaling SEP panic, memory bus abort, watchdog timeout, or physical tamper attempt.

secure_dram_window.allocation_semantics: 32 MB runtime execution window mapped from base physical 0x800000000, residing within the 97.6875 MB total TZ0 carveout

hardware_root_of_trust.architecture: Hardware-enforced secure execution domain with silicon-fused identities, independent cryptographic engines, and side-channel countermeasures.
boot_flow: 1. Fused Boot ROM verifies initial firmware stage signature via hardware RSA/ECDSA public root keys.
2. iBoot Stage-1 loads encrypted sep-firmware.v57.RELEASE.im4p into memory.
3. Hardware AES engine decrypts payload using silicon GID/UID keys without exposing keys to software.
4. SEPOS microkernel initializes in dedicated Secure DRAM carveout (TZ0), configuring DART-SEP and ASC mailbox.
5. SEPOS advertises endpoints to AP driver (AppleSEPManager) and engages Anti-Replay Token validation.
hardware_root_of_trust.silicon_fuse_array: eFuse OTP (One-Time Programmable) non-volatile macro storing UID, GID, production status, secure boot mode, and anti-rollback counters.

cipher_modes: AES-256-XTS (APFS storage encryption and Secure DRAM paging)
AES-256-GCM (Authenticated message encapsulation and backup bag encryption)
AES-256-CBC / AES-256-CTR (Legacy storage compatibility and biometric templates)
dedicated_aes_engine.key_registers: Hardware-internal write-only registers; key registers can be loaded from the hardware key ladder or TRNG but cannot be read by AP kernel, hypervisor, SPTM, TXM, or SEPOS firmware.

direct_hardware_bindings.role: Direct APFS media key unwrapping via hardware UID ladder, enabling disk decryption only on matching silicon.
Data Protection Class Key derivation (Class A through Class D) bound to user passcode and hardware UID.
Real-time, low-latency AES-XTS encryption of all data written from SEP caches to external Secure DRAM carveouts.

key_ladder.uid: Unique ID: 256-bit AES key permanently burned into silicon during manufacturing; completely unique to each individual device die and unreadable by any software.
key_ladder.gid: Group ID: 256-bit AES key shared across all chips of the same SoC family (t8150 / A18 Pro); utilized for universal firmware envelope decryption and base trust assertion.
key_ladder.derivation_algorithm: NIST SP 800-108 Key Derivation Function in Counter Mode using AES-CMAC and HMAC-SHA256 primitives.

ladder_hierarchy.name: Fused Silicon Root
ladder_hierarchy.hardware_gate: Hardwired to cryptographic core; zero software bus access.

ladder_hierarchy.name: Device Key Encryption Key (KEK)
ladder_hierarchy.role: Root key for encrypting file system keybags and device identity tokens.

classes.behavior: Keys discarded immediately upon device lock (com.apple.keystore.se.secret_drop); inaccessible until passcode entry.
Keys retained in memory for currently open files even when device is locked.
Keys retained in memory after first unlock until complete device reboot.
Encrypted with D-Key stored in Effaceable Storage; wiped instantly upon Erase All Content and Settings.

ladder_hierarchy.name: Hardware-Enforced Passcode Iteration
ladder_hierarchy.derivation: Hardware-accelerated scrypt/PBKDF2 iteration bound to fused UID; enforces exponential time delay (backoff delay) and maximum attempt thresholds in silicon.
ladder_hierarchy.role: Prevents offline brute-force attacks against user passcodes.

trng_drbg.entropy_source: On-chip True Random Number Generator utilizing thermal/avalanche junction noise within the Secure Enclave silicon boundary.
trng_drbg.validation: Continuous hardware health monitoring and statistical entropy verification conforming to NIST SP 800-90B standards.
trng_drbg.conditioning: NIST SP 800-90A compliant Deterministic Random Bit Generator (DRBG) operating in CTR_DRBG mode with AES-256.

kernel_prng_reseed.action: Periodically supplies high-entropy true random bytes from SEP TRNG to XNU kernel entropy pool via write_random(prng_entropy).

hardware_acceleration: NIST P-256 (secp256r1) Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA)
NIST P-384 (secp384r1) Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA)
RSA 2048 / 4096-bit modular exponentiation and PKCS#1 v1.5 / PSS verification
hardware_features: Constant-time point multiplication and modular inversion immune to timing side-channels
Hardware-enforced Secure In-Memory Key Acceleration (SIKA) (DeviceTree property sika-support: 0x1)
Zero-leakage register blinding and power analysis countermeasures
use_cases: Biometric Authentication: Pearl Face ID signature attestation and Secure Processor attestation tokens.
Apple Pay: Cryptographic token generation and cryptogram signing for EMV / Apple Pay transactions.
Secure Boot: Verification of Image4 manifest certificates and boot object digests.
Secure Key Exchange: Secure Identity Key (SIK) creation and ECDH key exchange.

anti_replay_nvram_storage.anti_rollback_counters: Fused silicon OTP monotonic counters enforcing firmware minimum version thresholds, preventing downgrades to vulnerable SEPOS builds.

anti_replay_tokens.art: Anti-Replay Tokens managed by AppleSEPARTStorage; validated against SEPOS commit hashes during boot handshake (ART_LOAD).
anti_replay_tokens.xart_gigalocker: External Anti-Replay Tokens managed by AppleSEPXART; synchronizes persistent epoch tables and locker storage for anti-replay verification.

nonce_generation.role: Boot ROM challenge nonce preventing replay of restore firmware manifests.
Dynamic session nonce invalidating replayed authentication attempts.
Boot Nonce / Challenge Nonce for Gigalocker epoch synchronization.

anti_replay_nvram_storage.nvram_persistence: Persistent Anti-Replay state committed to NVRAM (com.apple.System.sep.art) via AppleSEPARTService with synchronous flushing (kIONVRAMForceSyncNowPropertyKey).

effaceable_storage.architecture: Dedicated non-volatile flash storage blocks wired for single-operation erase.
effaceable_storage.d_key_locker: Stores Class D volume keys (d_key / s_key); obliterated instantly upon user request (com.apple.keystore.obliterate-d-key, DispatchUserClientEraseAllContentAndSettings), rendering all protected files unrecoverable within milliseconds.

out_of_line_buffer_protocol.allocation_model: Host-allocated, DART-mapped contiguous physical pages aligned to SEP page size (16 KB / 64 KB).
out_of_line_buffer_protocol.bounds_enforcement: SEPOS enforces min/max page limits advertised during discovery (ool_in_min_pages, ool_in_max_pages).
out_of_line_buffer_protocol.lifecycle: 1. Host driver calls cmsgSET_OOL_IN / cmsgSET_OOL_OUT; 2. Mailbox message transmits OOL descriptor index; 3. SEP DMA engine transfers bulk data directly via DART-SEP Stream 0/2; 4. Host receives completion interrupt on Line 304.

tightbeam_exclavecore_integration.architecture: Hardware-enforced secure microkernel IPC bridging ExclaveOS domains to SEPOS without relying on AP kernel trust.
tightbeam_exclavecore_integration.tbm_digests: Cryptographic binding via TBMDigests declared in sep-firmware.v57.RELEASE.im4p (tbms) containing 5 x 48-byte SHA-384 digests of verified ExclaveCore microkernel binaries.
tightbeam_exclavecore_integration.dart_isolation: ExclaveCore IPC traffic routes over dedicated DART-SEP Stream 2 (mapper-sep-exclave), enforcing stage-2 memory isolation from standard AP DMA.

rpc_interfaces.description: Establishes Tightbeam RPC endpoint session between ExclaveCore client and SEP proxy.
Processes asynchronous SEP outbox interrupt and routes incoming message words directly to ExclaveCore services.
Registers ExclaveCore protected memory buffers into SEP DART domain for zero-copy secure data exchange.
Revokes ExclaveCore buffer mappings upon completion of secure cryptographic operations.
Coordinates power state changes across ExclaveCore and SEPOS domains during system sleep transitions.
Confirms power transition completion and acknowledges standby readiness.
